inputs.content:
# Brightwork: should we launch an AI dispatch assistant? — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Brightwork sells field-service management software (scheduling, dispatch, quotes, invoicing) to HVAC,
plumbing and electrical contractors with 3–50 technicians. It has 9,800 customer accounts with an average of
6.2 office seats each (dispatchers and office staff) on the Core plan at $79 per seat per month: annual recurring
revenue (ARR) of $57.6M. Gross margin is 78%, annual logo churn 14%, net revenue retention 101%.

The product team has built **Dispatch Copilot**: AI that proposes a day's schedule, drafts quotes from
technician notes, and summarises customer calls. It ran as a free beta for 12 weeks.

**Decision maker:** CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team, at January 2027 planning.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and if so, how should it be packaged and priced?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- Raise net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028.
- Keep company gross margin at or above 75%.
- Engineering: 60 engineers in total. Launching Copilot needs 14 engineers for two quarters, which delays the
  rewrite of the technician mobile app by two quarters.

## 4. Current view inside the company

The Chief Product Officer proposes launching Copilot as a **paid add-on at $149 per account per month**: "Our
survey shows 46% of customers are likely to buy it. That is about $8M of new ARR in the first year."
The Head of Customer Success worries about the mobile app delay: "Mobile reliability is what customers complain
about."

## 5. Beta results (240 accounts, 12 weeks, volunteers)

**Table 1. Beta outcomes**

| Measure | Beta accounts | Matched non-beta accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Self-reported dispatcher hours saved per week | 4.1 | — |
| Change in jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour vs the prior 12 weeks | +11% | +2% |
| 90-day renewal rate | 97% | 93% |

- Beta accounts volunteered; they are larger (8.1 seats on average) and more active than the base.
- Usage is concentrated: the top 10% of beta accounts generated 58% of all AI requests.

**Table 2. AI requests per account per month (beta)**

|  | Requests per month |
|---|---|
| Median account | 1,900 |
| Mean account | 3,600 |
| Mean of the top 10% of accounts | 14,500 |

- Model inference cost: $0.009 per request under the current provider contract, fixed through December 2027.
  The provider's list prices fell 35% over the past 12 months.
- Running the feature also needs about $0.6M a year of platform, evaluation and support cost.

## 6. Pricing evidence

- **Survey** (October 2026, 610 customer admins): at $149 per account per month, 46% said they were "likely" or
  "very likely" to buy Copilot.
- **Paywall test** (last four weeks of the beta): 120 beta accounts were offered Copilot at $149 per account per
  month after the free period. 17 accounts (14%) bought it. Accounts that bought averaged 6,800 requests a month.
- **Tier option:** a new "Pro" plan that includes Copilot, priced $12 more per seat per month than Core. When
  Brightwork last launched a higher tier (2023), 33% of accounts moved to it within a year.

## 7. Competitor evidence

- **Routewise**, the closest competitor, launched AI scheduling **included in its Pro plan** in September 2026.
- Brightwork's win rate in deals where Routewise competed fell from 44% (Q1–Q2 2026) to 37% (Q3 2026).
  Brightwork has about 2,600 qualified new-customer opportunities a year, and Routewise competes in about 60% of
  them; a new account averages 6.2 seats on Core.
- In Q3 2026 lost deals, 31% of loss notes mention AI features.

## 8. Customer evidence

**Table 3. Main reason given by accounts that churned, 2026 (n = 1,190)**

| Reason | Share |
|---|---|
| Mobile app reliability | 27% |
| Price | 22% |
| Missing integrations | 15% |
| Went out of business / sold | 14% |
| Switched for AI features | 6% |
| Other | 16% |

- Top feature request in the 2026 customer survey: "a reliable technician mobile app" (38% rank it first);
  AI scheduling is ranked first by 19%.

## 9. Costs

- Engineering: 14 engineers for two quarters at a fully loaded $210,000 per engineer-year.

## 10. Other material

- **VP Sales memo:** "31% of our lost deals cite AI, so Copilot would recover about a third of the deals we lose to
  Routewise."
- **Survey method note:** the October survey went to all 9,800 account admins; 610 replied (6%). Respondents average
  9.4 seats, against 6.2 for all accounts.

## 11. Uncertainties

- Whether the productivity gain holds beyond volunteers.
- How fast inference prices fall after 2027.
- Whether Routewise's AI is the cause of the lower win rate or coincides with its price promotion in Q3 2026
  (Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3).

inputs.label: Choices made on the user's behalf (user unavailable during the build)
inputs.content: Audience: CEO and executive team deciding at January 2027 planning. Theme: navy. Pro usage allowance: 500 AI requests per seat per month, pooled per account (covers the mean beta account's 444 per seat). Stress case: half the 2023 tier take-up.

storyline.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, not as a $149 add-on, then start the mobile rewrite

exec_summary.text: Copilot is worth launching, but its productivity and competitive gains are smaller than they look

sub_points.text: Beta accounts gained 11% in jobs per dispatcher-hour, against 2% for matched ones
Losing ground to Routewise costs at most 109 deals a year, and a discount overlaps it

exec_summary.text: As a $149 add-on it would bring about $2.5M of ARR, not the $8M planned, and attract the costliest users

sub_points.text: Only 14% of beta accounts paid $149; 46% of survey respondents said they would
Buyers ran 1.9 times the mean account's requests; inference takes 41% of their price

exec_summary.text: A Pro plan at $12 more per seat adds about $2.9M of ARR and, with an allowance, keeps margin above 75%

sub_points.text: If 33% of accounts move up, as to the 2023 tier, Pro adds $2.89M of ARR
A 500-request allowance per seat holds company gross margin at 76.3%

exec_summary.text: The real cost is a two-quarter mobile delay: the rewrite must follow at once, watched by four gates

sub_points.text: Mobile drives 27% of churn against 6% for AI; the delay risks up to about $1.1M of ARR
If Pro take-up halves, 105% NRR needs the rewrite to cut mobile churn by about 40%

next_steps.action: Approve the Pro plan for a Q2 2027 launch at $91 per seat ($12 above Core) with 500 Copilot requests per seat
Price request packs above inference cost and design the Core-to-Pro upgrade offer
Fix the mobile rewrite to start the quarter the 14 Copilot engineers return
next_steps.owner: CTO and Head of Customer Success

next_steps.action: Build the gate dashboard: Pro take-up, cost per seat, mobile churn share, Routewise win rate
Open renegotiation of the inference contract ahead of its December 2027 end

constraints.item: Company gross margin at or above 75%
constraints.effect: Pro with a 500-request allowance holds 76.3%; uncapped at buyers' usage it falls to 75.1%, and free in Core breaks it at 74.3%; the allowance is part of the recommendation

constraints.item: 14 of 60 engineers for two quarters, delaying the mobile app rewrite by two quarters
constraints.effect: the delay puts up to $1.09M of ARR at risk; the exec summary names it as the launch's real cost and the rewrite is scheduled to follow at once

constraints.item: One-time build cost of $1.47M (14 engineers × half a year × $210,000)
constraints.effect: Pro repays it in about 1.2 years from $1.20M a year of contribution

constraints.item: $0.6M a year of platform, evaluation and support cost
constraints.effect: counted as cost of revenue in every margin and in the payback

constraints.item: Inference at $0.009 a request fixed through December 2027
constraints.effect: no price relief assumed in 2027; the 35% fall in list prices is an upside for the renegotiation
Pro alone reaches it in the base case (106%); the stress case needs the rewrite

alternatives.option: Launch as a paid add-on at $149 per account per month (CPO proposal)
alternatives.why: worth about $2.45M of ARR at the 14% who actually paid, not $8M; a flat price draws the heaviest users and charges for what Routewise includes

alternatives.option: Fix mobile first and launch Copilot two quarters later
alternatives.why: Pro is the only lever in the pack large enough to close the NRR gap, and Pro's $2.89M is 2.7 times the worst-case ARR the delay puts at risk; the rewrite is made the next priority, not dropped

alternatives.option: Include Copilot free in Core to match Routewise at no price
alternatives.why: no new ARR and company margin falls to 74.3% even at median beta use

failure_threshold.driver: Share of accounts moving to Pro
failure_threshold.threshold: below about 26% of accounts, Pro alone no longer closes the 4-percentage-point NRR gap; below 16.5%, the rewrite must remove more than 40% of mobile-reason churn
failure_threshold.range: Pro ARR low $1.44M (half the 2023 take-up) / base $2.89M (2023 take-up); NRR 103.5% / 106.0% from Pro alone

consistency.headline: Launch in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan with an allowance, not as a $149 add-on, and start the mobile rewrite right after
consistency.fix: the governing thought names the mobile rewrite as a condition, because the stress case reaches 105% only with it

gap.base_case: 106% with Pro alone at the 2023 take-up; 103.5% in the stress case

closers.option: Mobile rewrite started the quarter the 14 engineers return, removing about 40% of mobile-reason churn

cases.base: Pro adds $2.89M of ARR and lifts NRR to 106%, gross margin 76.3%
cases.stress: half the take-up adds $1.44M and NRR 103.5% from Pro; 105% needs the rewrite to remove about 40% of mobile-reason churn

gates.threshold: below 13% after six months (half the 26% break-even)
gates.response: plan on the stress case: protect the rewrite date and review Pro pricing
lower the allowance or raise request-pack prices

gates.threshold: above its 2026 level of 27% during the delay
gates.response: return engineers to the rewrite early

gates.threshold: still at or below 37% two quarters after launch
gates.response: treat losses as price-driven; respond to the discount rather than adding AI
